column1: # FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE on Android (keys in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Game profiles on Android")
# Unreal Engine 5.6.1 on SDK 20.5.17, update 1.0.1; 73,512 shaders, all translated. Its shader libraries are in the IoStore container, Oodle-compressed shader groups that the port
# decodes with the game's own Oodle on the device (porter device_ue: one round, 5,919 groups, 74,244 shaders in 44 s), so the port needs the device connected.
# Tested 2026-11-06 on the Legion Y700 (TB322FC, Snapdragon 8 Elite, Adreno 830, Android 16), docked (1920x1080): the brightness setting, the title, a new game (difficulty), the
# opening cinematic, the first road (walking, tutorials), the cutscene, the first battle's command menu; an autosave, and Continue from it after a restart (many times).
# 60 fps (the profile's fps_target): frame work p50 about 16.5 ms, GPU 10-13 ms in the field and the cinematic, 0-6 dropped frames per 300; 0 audio underruns; no red line.
# Its sprite particles' parameters (R32F buffer textures of 36-44 elements at offsets not a multiple of Adreno's 64) are read from an aligned copy on Qualcomm's driver,
# and through direct GPU buffer views on a driver with single-texel alignment, such as Turnip (gfx_vk_tex.c vk_tbuf_view, #243).
# Its particle compute shaders write R32UI / R32I buffer textures through float images: those get an integer variant (gfx_vk_shader.c spv_int_images), and the battle's
# haze and dust sprites (vertex shader fb570ef861debd17) draw since.
# The fires and smoke of the first road and the first battle (the battle tutorial's picture shows them) did not draw before #243 (5803c1c5). The cause was the shader
# translator, not the platform: it did not resolve the Niagara particle sprites' texture buffer handles (#243's Ryujinx BindlessElimination / Utils / ResourceManager fix).
# Ported again with #243 (2026-11-18, Legion Y700, this profile unchanged), they draw on Qualcomm's driver as in the tutorial picture. On Turnip fewer draw (the battle's
# left and right fires are missing, and a road fire showed as a black block for one frame); not explained yet: nothing turns Turnip's direct texel buffer views off.
# The game ignores command-line console variables (a shipping build: -dpcvars and -ini: through DM_GAME_ARGS_ADD changed nothing, r.ScreenPercentage included).
# First road, standing still (2026-11-06, docked): patches of fog on the road lit and went dark in turn. Its lights go into 32x32x32 volumes drawn slice by slice
# with additive blending; the core cleared only slice 0 of a layered pass, so the fog boxes that read them (1300ca45ddca3566) changed every frame: fixed in the core
# (gfx_vk_exec.c clear_color, every layer cleared; same on Qualcomm's driver and Turnip). The patches still went on and off after that (2026-11-08: two exact
# states, 37-56% of frames changed): each fog box's vertex shader reads its primitive from a table that a GPU radix sort builds every frame (a960d729840ecac2 clear,
# c0a487a5afca4bb9 histogram, 5854663e6002c250 scan, 98dee7b8a8eb9f9f scatter, 6 passes of 4 bits), and the translated scan and scatter read back a word they had
# just stored: the 32nd lane's prefix came out twice the 31st's, so the sort lost keys and the boxes drew from wrong entries in the frames whose batch order put
# them behind a big batch. Fixed in the translator (AstOptimizer: a load of writable memory is never moved to its use); after: 0 changes in 900 frames standing,
# 0 spike frames in 360 frames walking, the boxes drawn in every frame (DM_VK_X_FLAT_VS). Found by running Ryujinx's GLSL of the same jobs in a SIMT emulator.
